name: Firefox
hosting: Local app with optional cloud sync
encryption: HTTPS for web traffic; sync data encrypted in transit and at rest
summary: A mature browser with extensive privacy controls and a large extension ecosystem.
caveats: Some telemetry and sponsored/default content settings may require review; extensions can change the risk profile.

name: LibreWolf
encryption: HTTPS for web traffic
summary: A Firefox-based browser configured with privacy and security defaults.
caveats: Stricter defaults can break some sites; update cadence and extension choices still matter.

name: Brave
hosting: Local app with optional cloud features
encryption: HTTPS for web traffic
summary: Chromium-based browser with built-in tracker and ad blocking.
caveats: Optional rewards, AI, sync and other services add complexity; review settings and current policies.

name: Tor Browser
encryption: Tor routing plus HTTPS where available
summary: Designed to reduce tracking and make network-level correlation harder.
caveats: Does not make every activity anonymous; logging into personal accounts or opening downloaded files can identify you.

name: DuckDuckGo Search
encryption: HTTPS
summary: Search service focused on reducing personal search profiling.
caveats: A hosted service still sees requests and must be evaluated against its current privacy policy; results may rely on partners.

name: SearXNG
encryption: Depends on instance and upstream engines
summary: A metasearch engine that can be self-hosted to reduce dependence on a single search provider.
caveats: A public instance operator can observe queries; inspect instance policy or host your own.

name: Kagi Search
encryption: HTTPS
summary: Paid search designed around subscriptions rather than conventional search advertising.
caveats: Paid and hosted; check current retention, payment and account policies before adopting.

name: Proton Mail
encryption: End-to-end encryption for supported Proton-to-Proton and specific workflows; external email varies
summary: Encrypted email service with a privacy-focused account ecosystem.
caveats: Email to ordinary providers is not automatically end-to-end encrypted; metadata and recovery choices matter.

name: Tuta Mail
encryption: End-to-end encryption for supported Tuta mail; external recipients need supported workflow
summary: Encrypted email and calendar service with a privacy-oriented design.
caveats: Hosted provider; compatibility and encrypted communication with external recipients need planning.

name: Thunderbird
encryption: Depends on email provider and configuration; OpenPGP support available
summary: Open-source email client that lets you choose your own email provider.
caveats: A local client does not make an ordinary email provider private; server-side storage and transport policies still apply.

name: Signal
encryption: End-to-end encryption by default
summary: Private messaging and calling with end-to-end encryption by default.
caveats: Phone number is used for registration; backups, linked devices and contact discovery deserve review.

name: Element
encryption: End-to-end encryption in supported rooms and chats
summary: A Matrix-based messaging client with options to choose or operate a homeserver.
caveats: Security and metadata depend on homeserver, room settings, federation and device verification.

name: Session
encryption: End-to-end encryption
summary: Messaging designed to avoid requiring a phone number and reduce IP exposure to contacts.
caveats: Network design and decentralization trade-offs are different from mainstream messengers; assess current documentation and threat model.

name: Bitwarden
encryption: Vault data encrypted client-side; review account and recovery setup
summary: Cross-platform password manager with open-source clients and self-hosting options.
caveats: Self-hosting adds maintenance responsibility; protect recovery codes and master password.

name: KeePassXC
encryption: Encrypted local vault file
summary: Offline-first password manager storing credentials in a local database file.
caveats: You are responsible for secure backups and any syncing between devices; losing the database and key can mean losing access.

name: 1Password
encryption: Client-side encryption with account-specific security design
summary: Commercial password manager with cross-device vaults and team features.
caveats: Closed-source product and subscription; evaluate recovery, account dependencies and organisational policies.

name: Proton Drive
encryption: End-to-end encryption for supported stored files and sharing workflows
summary: Cloud file storage designed around client-side encryption and private sharing.
caveats: Hosted service; verify collaboration, recovery, preview and sharing limitations for your workflow.

name: Nextcloud
hosting: Self-hosted or hosted by a provider
encryption: HTTPS; at-rest and end-to-end encryption depend on configuration and features
summary: A self-hostable collaboration and file-sync platform for more control over data location.
caveats: Self-hosting transfers patching, backups, access control and uptime responsibilities to you.

name: Syncthing
encryption: TLS-protected transport with device identity
summary: Synchronises files directly between devices without a central cloud storage account.
caveats: Sync is not backup: deletions or ransomware can propagate; configure versioning and separate backups.

name: Cryptomator
hosting: Encrypts files before they are stored in chosen cloud folder
account: No Cryptomator account required for basic desktop use
encryption: Client-side file and filename encryption
summary: Adds client-side encryption to files stored with a cloud provider or on local storage.
caveats: Protect vault passwords and recovery material; file sizes and access patterns may remain visible.

name: Ente Photos
kind: Open source clients and hosted service
hosting: Hosted service; self-hosting options may vary by component
encryption: End-to-end encrypted photo storage according to provider documentation
summary: Photo backup and sharing service designed around end-to-end encryption.
caveats: Review current self-hosting support, sharing workflow, account recovery and device compatibility.

name: Immich
encryption: HTTPS and storage protection depend on deployment; not automatically end-to-end encrypted
summary: Self-hosted photo and video management with mobile backup clients.
caveats: Requires maintenance and a separate backup plan; do not expose an unpatched server directly to the internet.

name: LibreOffice
encryption: Local files; document encryption options depend on format and settings
summary: Offline-capable office suite for documents, spreadsheets and presentations.
caveats: Cloud collaboration is not built into the core in the same way as hosted office suites; document metadata may persist.

name: Standard Notes
hosting: Hosted sync; local use varies by client and plan
encryption: End-to-end encryption according to product design
summary: Notes application focused on encrypted syncing and long-term note portability.
caveats: Check export formats, plan limitations and current hosting policies before moving a large archive.

name: Logseq
encryption: Local files; sync protection depends on chosen service
summary: Outliner and knowledge-management app that can keep a graph in local files.
caveats: Plugin permissions and optional sync services can change the privacy profile; maintain portable backups.

name: Obsidian
kind: Proprietary app with local Markdown files
hosting: Local vault; sync is optional paid service or third party
encryption: Local files; Obsidian Sync offers encryption features subject to configuration
summary: Knowledge-management app using local Markdown files and a broad plugin ecosystem.
caveats: Core app is not open source; community plugins run code and should be chosen carefully.

name: Ollama
hosting: Runs models locally; optional network features depend on use
encryption: Local API is not an internet-facing security boundary; secure any remote exposure yourself
summary: Runs supported language models locally on your own computer.
caveats: Model downloads require network access; hardware limits apply and local inference does not guarantee that every extension or app stays offline.

name: LM Studio
hosting: Local model inference; downloads and optional integrations use network
account: Not generally required for local inference
encryption: Local API access controls and network exposure require attention
summary: Desktop interface for downloading and running compatible language models locally.
caveats: Proprietary software; local inference is not the same as a complete air-gapped setup.

name: Linux Mint
encryption: Disk encryption available during installation depending on edition and setup
summary: Desktop Linux distribution with a familiar interface and long-term support releases.
caveats: Hardware and driver compatibility vary; full-disk encryption and backups should be planned at installation.

name: Debian
hosting: Local operating system or self-managed server
encryption: Disk encryption options available; security depends on installation and updates
summary: Community-developed operating system known for broad hardware support and stable releases.
caveats: Some desktop conveniences may require manual setup; administrators must apply updates and configure services.

name: Proton VPN
encryption: Encrypted VPN tunnel; does not provide end-to-end encryption for destination services
summary: VPN service with open-source clients and published privacy and security material.
caveats: A VPN shifts trust from the local network or ISP to the VPN operator; it does not make browsing anonymous by itself.

name: Mullvad VPN
encryption: Encrypted VPN tunnel
summary: VPN provider emphasizing minimal account information and privacy-oriented operations.
caveats: A VPN does not prevent account-based tracking, browser fingerprinting or tracking by websites you log into.

name: AdGuard DNS
encryption: Encrypted DNS options supported; configuration-dependent
summary: DNS filtering service for blocking selected ads, trackers and malicious domains.
caveats: DNS filtering is not a VPN and cannot block every tracker; DNS operator can observe resolver queries.

name: OpenStreetMap
hosting: Public service; data can be downloaded and self-hosted
encryption: HTTPS on public site; app privacy depends on chosen client
summary: Collaborative open map data that powers many independent mapping applications.
caveats: The public website and third-party apps have different privacy practices; choose an offline-capable client if needed.

name: Organic Maps
encryption: Offline maps reduce network exposure during navigation; optional features may differ
summary: Offline maps and navigation built around OpenStreetMap data.
caveats: Map downloads need connectivity; app features and platform availability should be checked for your device.

name: LocalSend
encryption: Encrypted transfer according to project documentation; network trust still matters
summary: Transfers files between nearby devices over a local network without a cloud account.
caveats: Confirm device identity and use trusted networks; local-network access can expose devices to other network participants.

name: Joplin
hosting: Local notes with optional sync targets
encryption: End-to-end encryption available for synchronisation when configured
summary: Open-source note-taking app with import/export and flexible synchronisation options.
caveats: E2EE must be enabled and configured for sync; local backups remain important.
